world.title: Trump seeks permanent Iran nuclear deal as Gulf conflict persists
world.summary: President Donald Trump said on Nov. 21 that he wants a “permanent” agreement with Iran to prevent it from obtaining nuclear weapons and argued that no future U.S. president should be able to reverse that commitment. In a Fox News interview, Trump accused Tehran of breaking past agreements and said regime change was not
world.content: President Donald Trump said on Nov. 21 that he wants a “permanent” agreement with Iran to prevent it from obtaining nuclear weapons and argued that no future U.S. president should be able to reverse that commitment. In a Fox News interview, Trump accused Tehran of breaking past agreements and said regime change was not his priority, though he referred to dealing with successive groups of Iranian leaders. Iranian Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi said Tehran remained in contact with mediators and wanted an agreement that would prevent another war. Iran has also demanded assurances that Washington is negotiating seriously; its stated conditions include ending the conflict on all fronts, unfreezing Iranian assets, lifting oil sanctions and ending the U.S. counter-blockade of Iranian ports. A Qatari delegation held talks in Tehran on Friday, while U.S. and Israeli officials are considering a renewed assault, CBS News reported, citing people familiar with the matter. Trump has said he is not rushing a decision on his next military move and could wait until 2027.
world.image_alt: Trump seeks permanent Iran nuclear deal as Gulf conflict persists

world.title: Israeli fire kills four in Gaza, including three in vehicle carrying food
world.summary: Israeli fire killed four Palestinians in Gaza on Saturday, including three in a drone strike on a vehicle carrying food in Tel al-Hawa, Gaza City, and one in Jabalia al-Balad, the Gaza civil defence agency said. Several people were wounded in the vehicle strike. Al-Shifa Hospital received all four bodies. The Israeli m
world.content: Israeli fire killed four Palestinians in Gaza on Saturday, including three in a drone strike on a vehicle carrying food in Tel al-Hawa, Gaza City, and one in Jabalia al-Balad, the Gaza civil defence agency said. Several people were wounded in the vehicle strike. Al-Shifa Hospital received all four bodies. The Israeli military said it targeted Islamic Jihad operatives using the vehicle to transport food and supplies and that the vehicle had no visible humanitarian-aid markings. The charity World Central Kitchen said the vehicle was not affiliated with it. The driver had previously worked for the charity, but the other two occupants were not its workers. A witness told Reuters the vehicle was about to distribute food and drink to children when it was hit.
world.image_alt: Israeli fire kills four in Gaza, including three in vehicle carrying food

world.title: Pentagon restricts US-Canada defense ties in classified memo
world.summary: U.S. Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth issued a classified directive restricting military cooperation with Canada. Republican Sen. Mike Rounds said it limits informal and social contact between the countries’ military personnel. The Washington Post reported that the memo circulated last week but said it had not seen the d
world.content: U.S. Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth issued a classified directive restricting military cooperation with Canada. Republican Sen. Mike Rounds said it limits informal and social contact between the countries’ military personnel. The Washington Post reported that the memo circulated last week but said it had not seen the document. The directive’s full scope remains unclear. The Pentagon says the guidance refocuses engagement on U.S. defense priorities and will not affect military intelligence sharing, the North American Aerospace Defense Command (NORAD) or cooperation through the North Atlantic Treaty Organization (NATO). Canadian Defence Minister David McGuinty said he had not seen the memo and had observed no change in military cooperation. President Donald Trump has imposed tariffs on Canadian goods, criticized Canada’s defense spending and repeatedly suggested that Canada become a U.S. state. The Pentagon paused a longstanding bilateral defense forum in May, while Canada says it has reached NATO’s 2% spending target and plans to increase defense spending to 5% of gross domestic product by 2035.
world.image_alt: Pentagon restricts US-Canada defense ties in classified memo

world.title: Nigeria boat capsize kills 24 mourners as search continues
world.summary: A boat carrying mourners to a funeral sank Friday, Nov. 20, in Bayelsa State, southern Nigeria, killing at least 24 people. Manzo Ezekiel, a spokesman for Nigeria’s National Emergency Management Agency, said 24 bodies had been recovered by Saturday and search-and-rescue operations were continuing. Police said 24 people
world.content: A boat carrying mourners to a funeral sank Friday, Nov. 20, in Bayelsa State, southern Nigeria, killing at least 24 people. Manzo Ezekiel, a spokesman for Nigeria’s National Emergency Management Agency, said 24 bodies had been recovered by Saturday and search-and-rescue operations were continuing. Police said 24 people survived and received medical assistance; officials have not confirmed how many passengers were aboard or how many remain missing. Police spokesman Musa Mohammed said preliminary findings pointed to a mechanical problem. He said passengers asked the operator to head toward shore, but alleged that the operator refused and later fled. The boat’s manager was taken into custody. Al Jazeera reported that some residents told Reuters they believed at least 300 people were aboard, but authorities have not confirmed that figure. The boat was travelling from Ayama to Ukubie for a burial ceremony. Two children were among the first four bodies recovered on Friday. President Bola Tinubu expressed condolences as local search-and-rescue efforts continued.
world.image_alt: Nigeria boat capsize kills 24 mourners as search continues

world.title: Indonesia factory fire kills three, leaves 36 workers missing
world.summary: A fire at the PT Fonusa Agung Mulia candy factory in Cikande, Serang district, killed three people and left 36 workers unaccounted for as rescuers searched the damaged building on Sunday, Nov. 22. The factory makes Milkita, a milk-based candy brand. The National Search and Rescue Agency said 15 people were found alive,
world.content: A fire at the PT Fonusa Agung Mulia candy factory in Cikande, Serang district, killed three people and left 36 workers unaccounted for as rescuers searched the damaged building on Sunday, Nov. 22. The factory makes Milkita, a milk-based candy brand. The National Search and Rescue Agency said 15 people were found alive, including four injured workers taken for medical care. The blaze began Saturday afternoon, and firefighters were still battling flames and cooling parts of the three-story facility more than 12 hours later. Banten Governor Andra Soni said about 60 people were believed to have been inside when the fire began; authorities had not confirmed whether all 36 missing workers were inside. Relatives gathered outside the factory awaiting news. Authorities have not established the cause of the fire, which survivors said started near a cooling unit on the third floor. Search teams were checking sections where people might be trapped while firefighters continued to control remaining hot spots.
world.image_alt: Indonesia factory fire kills three, leaves 36 workers missing

world.title: British endurance swimmer completes 15-kilometer Hormuz swim, warns of pollution from war
world.summary: British endurance swimmer Lewis Pugh, the United Nations Environment Programme’s Patron of the Oceans, completed a 15-kilometer swim along Oman’s Strait of Hormuz coast over three days between Nov. 15 and Nov. 18 to draw attention to environmental damage from the Iran war. He called for the fighting to stop, the strait
world.content: British endurance swimmer Lewis Pugh, the United Nations Environment Programme’s Patron of the Oceans, completed a 15-kilometer swim along Oman’s Strait of Hormuz coast over three days between Nov. 15 and Nov. 18 to draw attention to environmental damage from the Iran war. He called for the fighting to stop, the strait to reopen and pollution to be cleaned up. Pugh said he heard explosions about 30 minutes after entering the water, when an oil tanker was hit roughly four kilometers away. He later saw a gas carrier engulfed in flames. Iran has said it attacked vessels it considered to be using unauthorized routes through the strait. Pugh warned that oil and chemical pollution from damaged ships could harm wildlife, coral reefs, mangroves and coastlines for years. He described the strait as a living habitat as well as a shipping route and said the contamination could be difficult to remove.
world.image_alt: British endurance swimmer completes 15-kilometer Hormuz swim, warns of pollution from war

world.title: Eisenkot invites Netanyahu’s Likud to talks to form Israeli government
world.summary: Former Israeli military chief Gadi Eisenkot, leader of the centrist Yashar party, has invited caretaker Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu’s Likud party to intensive coalition talks beginning Sunday, Nov. 22. President Isaac Herzog tasked Eisenkot with forming a government after the Oct. 27 election left no bloc with a
world.content: Former Israeli military chief Gadi Eisenkot, leader of the centrist Yashar party, has invited caretaker Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu’s Likud party to intensive coalition talks beginning Sunday, Nov. 22. President Isaac Herzog tasked Eisenkot with forming a government after the Oct. 27 election left no bloc with a majority in the 120-seat Knesset, Israel’s parliament. Eisenkot’s mandate expires Dec. 6. Netanyahu’s bloc holds 53 seats, Eisenkot’s opposition bloc 48, and Arab-led parties 19. Coalition leaders are divided over whether to include ultra-Orthodox parties, seek Arab-party support or form a unity government with Likud. Likud says a unity arrangement must end political boycotts of Netanyahu and exclude Arab parties; Eisenkot has said he could work with Likud lawmakers but not serve under Netanyahu. Former Prime Minister Naftali Bennett supports a unity government led by Eisenkot but ruled out joining Netanyahu or his bloc. Yisrael Beytenu leader Avigdor Liberman favors negotiating with ultra-Orthodox parties, while Democrats leader Yair Golan has advocated a minority government relying on Arab-party support. Eisenkot has said he will not let talks drag on and may put a minority national-emergency government to a parliamentary vote if broader negotiations fail.
world.image_alt: Eisenkot invites Netanyahu’s Likud to talks to form Israeli government

world.title: Iran strikes Bahrain as Hormuz tanker attacks deepen Gulf standoff
world.summary: Bahrain said an Iranian attack caused a fire at a civilian industrial facility on Saturday, Nov. 21, causing material damage but no injuries. Iran’s Revolutionary Guard Corps said it had instead targeted U.S. positions at the Al-Riffa and Awali bases with missiles and drones, claiming it hit two Patriot air-defense rad
world.content: Bahrain said an Iranian attack caused a fire at a civilian industrial facility on Saturday, Nov. 21, causing material damage but no injuries. Iran’s Revolutionary Guard Corps said it had instead targeted U.S. positions at the Al-Riffa and Awali bases with missiles and drones, claiming it hit two Patriot air-defense radars. Bahrain reported intercepting several incoming attacks, and the U.S. military had not confirmed damage to its bases. Projectiles also struck two tankers transiting the Strait of Hormuz, according to the U.K. Maritime Trade Operations center. Iran’s army said another vessel caught fire after hitting a mine in a restricted area, while the U.S. military said it had cleared mines from the main routes. The strait carried about one-fifth of global oil before the war. Iran has sought to restrict shipping through it, while the United States has imposed a counter-blockade of Iranian ports. Iranian Deputy Foreign Minister Kazem Gharibabadi said a Qatari delegation held two hours of mediation talks in Tehran on Friday. Iranian Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi said Iran would not discuss reopening the strait until its demands—including an end to the war and U.S. blockade—were met. Iran’s electricity company said rolling power cuts would begin Sunday, Nov. 22, citing fuel supply conditions.
world.image_alt: Iran strikes Bahrain as Hormuz tanker attacks deepen Gulf standoff

business.title: Bitcoin rebounds above $60,000 after hitting two-year low
business.summary: Bitcoin climbed more than 8% to about $59,952 on Saturday after falling to $55,251.60, its lowest level since September 2024, and briefly rose above $60,000. The rebound followed a sharp selloff that pushed the price below $57,742 on Friday for the first time since September 2024. Investors have been selling risk asset
business.content: Bitcoin climbed more than 8% to about $59,952 on Saturday after falling to $55,251.60, its lowest level since September 2024, and briefly rose above $60,000. The rebound followed a sharp selloff that pushed the price below $57,742 on Friday for the first time since September 2024. Investors have been selling risk assets as doubts about artificial-intelligence spending, rising borrowing costs, a stronger U.S. dollar and higher real yields weighed on technology shares and cryptocurrencies. U.S. spot bitcoin exchange-traded funds recorded about $1.1 billion in net withdrawals over the week, while liquidations of leveraged crypto positions totaled about $1.8 billion in 24 hours, mostly bets on rising prices. QCP Capital said a sustained recovery would require steadier technology stocks and renewed institutional investment; U.S. markets were due to reopen Monday, Nov. 23.
business.image_alt: Bitcoin rebounds above $60,000 after hitting two-year low

business.title: Nvidia faces leadership and China-market risks after Huang
business.summary: Nvidia co-founder Jensen Huang stepped down as chief executive last week, leaving former finance chief Colette Kress as interim CEO while the board seeks a permanent successor. His departure followed disclosure of an affair with Alice Huang, a Chinese woman whom the United States suspects of espionage; China has reject
business.content: Nvidia co-founder Jensen Huang stepped down as chief executive last week, leaving former finance chief Colette Kress as interim CEO while the board seeks a permanent successor. His departure followed disclosure of an affair with Alice Huang, a Chinese woman whom the United States suspects of espionage; China has rejected the accusation. Coverage also reported U.S. intelligence concerns about alleged efforts to obtain export-restricted Nvidia chips through an intermediary. The leadership change coincided with a U.S. rule requiring overseas neocloud providers—companies that rent computing capacity—to obtain licenses to serve Chinese customers, closing a route around restrictions on direct chip sales. Neocloud firms also face tighter financing: Kress said Nvidia's guarantees depend on projects securing funding and completing construction, and analyst Gil Luria said lenders are already pulling back.
business.image_alt: Nvidia faces leadership and China-market risks after Huang

business.title: Investigation links Nvidia chip network to suppliers tied to China’s military
business.summary: A Financial Times investigation traced a network associated with former Megaspeed executive Alice Huang that allegedly routed Nvidia artificial-intelligence chips toward Chinese users through corporate intermediaries, offshore companies and a suspected smuggling connection in Cambodia. The New York Times separately lin
business.content: A Financial Times investigation traced a network associated with former Megaspeed executive Alice Huang that allegedly routed Nvidia artificial-intelligence chips toward Chinese users through corporate intermediaries, offshore companies and a suspected smuggling connection in Cambodia. The New York Times separately linked companies associated with Huang to suppliers connected to China’s military. A confidential analysis cited by the Times estimated that about $3.6 billion in Chinese state funding flowed through firms tied to her family or associates, but said it was unclear whether the military used the computing power. The reported network included Aivres, the U.S. unit of Chinese server maker Inspur, and Megaspeed, which investigators said served as an offshore customer for chip access. Nvidia said it blocked Megaspeed and a subsidiary in 2025 and restricted sales to Aivres. The reports describe allegations and corporate links but do not establish that every company knew of or participated in illicit shipments. Nvidia said it had stopped shipping H200 chips to China and had not shipped and would not ship them to Century Litong’s Hong Kong unit, which appeared in congressional license files.
business.image_alt: Investigation links Nvidia chip network to suppliers tied to China’s military

business.title: AI stock rout pushes U.S. indexes into correction, erasing gains
business.summary: U.S. stocks sold off sharply during the week as investors questioned whether spending on artificial intelligence would deliver expected returns. The Nasdaq fell 10% for the week, while the S&P 500 and Dow entered correction territory, down at least 10% from recent highs. AI and chip shares led Friday’s losses; Nvidia f
business.content: U.S. stocks sold off sharply during the week as investors questioned whether spending on artificial intelligence would deliver expected returns. The Nasdaq fell 10% for the week, while the S&P 500 and Dow entered correction territory, down at least 10% from recent highs. AI and chip shares led Friday’s losses; Nvidia fell about 14%, and newly listed Anthropic lost 8.5%. Investors cited the prospect of slower data-center construction, tighter financing, stricter regulation and weaker technology-company profit growth. Nvidia has invested in companies including Anthropic and CoreWeave and lends to AI firms that buy its chips, NPR reported. CoreWeave is also borrowing heavily to build data centers, raising concerns that trouble at one company could spread through the financing chain. Some analysts say the risk is less severe than in the dot-com bust because established companies are driving much of today’s AI investment, while others question whether valuations can be justified. In China, three technology-focused indexes have shed a combined $1.7 trillion in market value since June, Bloomberg reported.
business.image_alt: AI stock rout pushes U.S. indexes into correction, erasing gains

business.title: Bayer’s $7.25 billion Roundup deal leaves lawsuits and appeals ahead
business.summary: Bayer’s court-approved settlement of up to $7.25 billion over claims that its Roundup weedkiller caused non-Hodgkin lymphoma leaves about 200 federal cases outside the deal, and the ruling could be appealed. The settlement covers people already diagnosed and some who develop the cancer after exposure to Roundup; Bayer
business.content: Bayer’s court-approved settlement of up to $7.25 billion over claims that its Roundup weedkiller caused non-Hodgkin lymphoma leaves about 200 federal cases outside the deal, and the ruling could be appealed. The settlement covers people already diagnosed and some who develop the cancer after exposure to Roundup; Bayer denies that the product causes cancer. A Missouri judge approved the agreement after a June U.S. Supreme Court decision restricted state failure-to-warn claims, making lawsuits harder to pursue. Bayer says the deal aims to reduce risks from pending and future litigation, but the scientific and regulatory dispute over glyphosate remains unresolved. The Environmental Protection Agency is reviewing health evidence with the Department of Health and Human Services, with findings expected next year.
business.image_alt: Bayer’s $7.25 billion Roundup deal leaves lawsuits and appeals ahead

business.title: US tech outages spur emergency buying as AI accelerates bug discovery
business.summary: A series of US technology failures from Nov. 12 to 17 disrupted commercial flights, banking transactions, Microsoft services, Apple apps and a National Security Agency network, but officials and technical findings have not established a coordinated cyberattack. Reported causes include a faulty Microsoft update, newly i
business.content: A series of US technology failures from Nov. 12 to 17 disrupted commercial flights, banking transactions, Microsoft services, Apple apps and a National Security Agency network, but officials and technical findings have not established a coordinated cyberattack. Reported causes include a faulty Microsoft update, newly installed aviation network equipment, an internal Apple update and problems during NSA maintenance. AI tools are helping researchers find software vulnerabilities faster, prompting rapid patching that can itself introduce failures. Consumer spending at emergency-product brands jumped about 400% during Nov. 12-17 from a year earlier, according to card data analyzed for CNBC. Palo Alto Networks CEO Nikesh Arora estimated that addressing technical debt could take another 12 to 18 months.
business.image_alt: US tech outages spur emergency buying as AI accelerates bug discovery

business.title: SEC investigates Nvidia’s accounting practices
business.summary: The U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission is investigating Nvidia’s accounting practices, according to people briefed on the inquiry. The investigation is at an early stage and could end without charges. Its precise focus remains unclear, including whether it concerns Nvidia’s geographic revenue reporting or financin
business.content: The U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission is investigating Nvidia’s accounting practices, according to people briefed on the inquiry. The investigation is at an early stage and could end without charges. Its precise focus remains unclear, including whether it concerns Nvidia’s geographic revenue reporting or financing arrangements with AI companies and data-center projects. Nvidia interim chief executive Colette Kress said the company would be more selective about financing deals in the AI industry. The SEC’s enforcement division recently created a financial-reporting and accounting unit. The Justice Department is reviewing Nvidia’s proposed $12.9 billion acquisition of open-source platform Hugging Face as part of a broader antitrust investigation.

business.title: Trump renews push for 10% credit card rate cap with Democrats
business.summary: President Donald Trump said he would work with the incoming Democratic-controlled Congress to cap credit card interest rates at 10%, reviving a 2024 campaign pledge he did not fulfill after banks opposed the plan and congressional Republicans showed little interest. The cap would be well below the 22.2% median rate rep
business.content: President Donald Trump said he would work with the incoming Democratic-controlled Congress to cap credit card interest rates at 10%, reviving a 2024 campaign pledge he did not fulfill after banks opposed the plan and congressional Republicans showed little interest. The cap would be well below the 22.2% median rate reported in an August New York Federal Reserve survey. Sen. Elizabeth Warren, a Massachusetts Democrat expected to chair the Senate Banking Committee, welcomed the renewed push. Banks and card companies argue a cap could lead them to restrict credit for lower-income and less creditworthy borrowers or reduce rewards. Researchers cited in the coverage estimate a 10% cap could save consumers about $100 billion a year in interest, with card issuers remaining profitable but offering fewer perks. Democrats are due to take control of both chambers in January, but it is unclear whether they will prioritize the measure.
business.image_alt: Trump renews push for 10% credit card rate cap with Democrats

science.title: Court halts Army plan to detonate five tons of lead azide in Iowa
science.summary: A federal court temporarily halted the U.S. Army’s plan to detonate 68 drums of degraded lead azide at the Iowa Army Ammunition Plant near Middletown after environmental groups challenged an emergency permit and raised concerns about lead dust spreading across Iowa and western Illinois. The Army had rescheduled the bla
science.content: A federal court temporarily halted the U.S. Army’s plan to detonate 68 drums of degraded lead azide at the Iowa Army Ammunition Plant near Middletown after environmental groups challenged an emergency permit and raised concerns about lead dust spreading across Iowa and western Illinois. The Army had rescheduled the blasts for Monday, Nov. 23, after objections from the public and elected officials; the court’s pause leaves it unclear whether they can proceed that day. The Army says the material became more sensitive to shock and friction after liquid evaporated during prolonged storage, making transport hazardous and controlled detonation the safest immediate option. The plan calls for wetting the soil and using sand barriers to limit airborne particles, but the amount of lead likely to escape remains uncertain. University of Iowa researchers and the U.S. Environmental Protection Agency planned to sample air and surfaces. The EPA was expected to respond to the lawsuit by Nov. 22, while the judge set no date for further action.
science.image_alt: Court halts Army plan to detonate five tons of lead azide in Iowa

science.title: Lean and Mathlib groups back formal validity of claimed Riemann proof
science.summary: The Lean and Mathlib communities said they had independently checked the formalized code for Anthropic mathematician Levent Alpöge’s claimed proof of the Riemann hypothesis, a problem about prime-number distribution. Alpöge developed the proof with the company’s Claude AI. In a Nov. 21 statement, the communities said t
science.content: The Lean and Mathlib communities said they had independently checked the formalized code for Anthropic mathematician Levent Alpöge’s claimed proof of the Riemann hypothesis, a problem about prime-number distribution. Alpöge developed the proof with the company’s Claude AI. In a Nov. 21 statement, the communities said they had “full confidence” in the proof. Their review checked whether the formal statement matches the Riemann hypothesis, whether the code compiles, whether it uses the theorem already defined in Mathlib and whether the argument is logically valid. The endorsement does not yet make the result an officially accepted solution: the Clay Mathematics Institute’s rules require publication in a peer-reviewed journal and two years of scrutiny, and the institute still lists the problem as unsolved. Alpöge said he plans to provide a human-readable account of the work.
science.image_alt: Lean and Mathlib groups back formal validity of claimed Riemann proof

science.title: Ebola death toll in Congo exceeds 5,700 as response lags
science.summary: An Ebola outbreak in the Democratic Republic of the Congo has surpassed 11,700 confirmed cases and 5,700 deaths as of Nov. 19, making it the country’s largest and deadliest. Cases have also been reported in Uganda, Kenya and Nigeria. The Bundibugyo strain is driving the outbreak, and no approved vaccine or targeted tre
science.content: An Ebola outbreak in the Democratic Republic of the Congo has surpassed 11,700 confirmed cases and 5,700 deaths as of Nov. 19, making it the country’s largest and deadliest. Cases have also been reported in Uganda, Kenya and Nigeria. The Bundibugyo strain is driving the outbreak, and no approved vaccine or targeted treatment is available for it. Health workers say early cases can be difficult to identify because initial symptoms resemble those of other illnesses. Late detection, population movement and mistrust of response teams have hindered containment, while attacks on health workers and burial teams have further complicated the response. On Nov. 17, health workers in Butembo, North Kivu, escalated a month-long strike over unpaid wages and bonuses, halting even minimum service at treatment centers.
science.image_alt: Ebola death toll in Congo exceeds 5,700 as response lags

science.title: COP31 draft acknowledges 1.5C overshoot as IPCC schedule remains disputed
science.summary: A third draft of the COP31 agreement, circulated in Antalya on Sunday, says for the first time in a climate summit text that the world is on track to miss the Paris Agreement’s 1.5C warming limit. The draft acknowledges an approaching period of “overshoot”; scientists warn that passing the threshold will expose million
science.content: A third draft of the COP31 agreement, circulated in Antalya on Sunday, says for the first time in a climate summit text that the world is on track to miss the Paris Agreement’s 1.5C warming limit. The draft acknowledges an approaching period of “overshoot”; scientists warn that passing the threshold will expose millions more people to sea-level rise and extreme heat. Negotiators remain divided over when to publish the next assessment from the Intergovernmental Panel on Climate Change (IPCC), the UN body that evaluates climate science. The European Union, Brazil, the United Kingdom and island states want it ready for the 2028 global stocktake, while Russia, Iran, India and Saudi Arabia favor 2029. Researchers say the earlier timetable is feasible, while opponents cite risks to research quality and participation. Delegates also disagree over the draft’s call to accelerate carbon capture and storage, a technology critics say is costly and has a limited record of cutting emissions. The session scheduled to consider approval of the text was delayed on Sunday morning, and no final agreement had been adopted at that point.
science.image_alt: COP31 draft acknowledges 1.5C overshoot as IPCC schedule remains disputed

science.title: European-Japanese BepiColombo enters Mercury orbit ahead of two-probe science mission
science.summary: BepiColombo, a joint mission of the European Space Agency and Japan Aerospace Exploration Agency, entered orbit around Mercury on Nov. 21, completing an eight-year journey and becoming the second mission to orbit the planet. The two orbiters remain attached; they are scheduled to separate on Dec. 9–10 and take up diffe
science.content: BepiColombo, a joint mission of the European Space Agency and Japan Aerospace Exploration Agency, entered orbit around Mercury on Nov. 21, completing an eight-year journey and becoming the second mission to orbit the planet. The two orbiters remain attached; they are scheduled to separate on Dec. 9–10 and take up different polar orbits, with science operations due to begin in April 2027. The mission will use the European Mercury Planetary Orbiter and Japan’s Mercury Magnetospheric Orbiter, called Mio, to study Mercury from separate vantage points. Their instruments are designed to examine the planet’s surface and interior, its magnetic field and the thin gas envelope around it, including how the magnetic field interacts with the solar wind. Controllers in Germany confirmed the spacecraft’s capture several hours after a series of braking thruster firings, with the spacecraft about 152 million kilometers away. A propulsion-system problem delayed BepiColombo’s arrival from December 2025. Its nominal science mission is planned to last one Earth year, with an extension through 2029.
science.image_alt: European-Japanese BepiColombo enters Mercury orbit ahead of two-probe science mission

sports.title: A-Lim Kim takes one-shot lead as Korda eyes Hall of Fame
sports.summary: South Korea’s A-Lim Kim will enter the final round of the LPGA’s CME Group Tour Championship at 18 under, one shot ahead of Thailand’s Jeeno Thitikul and Japan’s Yuri Yoshida. Kim shot a three-under 69 in Saturday’s third round in Naples, Florida, with two late bogeys trimming her advantage. The winner of the season-en
sports.content: South Korea’s A-Lim Kim will enter the final round of the LPGA’s CME Group Tour Championship at 18 under, one shot ahead of Thailand’s Jeeno Thitikul and Japan’s Yuri Yoshida. Kim shot a three-under 69 in Saturday’s third round in Naples, Florida, with two late bogeys trimming her advantage. The winner of the season-ending tournament earns $4 million from an $11 million purse. World No. 1 Nelly Korda shot a seven-under 65 to reach 16 under, two shots behind Kim. A victory would give Korda the final point she needs for induction into the LPGA Hall of Fame. Thitikul, the two-time defending champion, and Yoshida, who made six birdies without a bogey, are tied for second. The final round is scheduled for Sunday.
sports.image_alt: A-Lim Kim takes one-shot lead as Korda eyes Hall of Fame

sports.title: Fernandes puts Manchester United contract talks on hold as Milan watches
sports.summary: Manchester United captain Bruno Fernandes says the club has offered him a new contract, but he has paused negotiations because he believes the team’s priority must be winning again. His current contract runs through June 2027, with United holding an option to extend it by a year. Chief executive Omar Berrada confirmed
sports.content: Manchester United captain Bruno Fernandes says the club has offered him a new contract, but he has paused negotiations because he believes the team’s priority must be winning again. His current contract runs through June 2027, with United holding an option to extend it by a year. Chief executive Omar Berrada confirmed the club is discussing a new deal with Fernandes, while new head coach Mauricio Pochettino has said Fernandes will remain captain. AC Milan is monitoring the situation, and other clubs have also been linked with the 32-year-old midfielder; reports differ on how far any approaches have gone. Reports say Fernandes wants terms through 2030, while United would prefer a shorter extension. Pochettino is expected to speak with Fernandes about his future at the club.
sports.image_alt: Fernandes puts Manchester United contract talks on hold as Milan watches

sports.title: Verstappen wins Las Vegas Grand Prix after 35 lead changes
sports.summary: Red Bull driver Max Verstappen won the Las Vegas Grand Prix on Saturday, claiming his 75th Formula 1 victory in a race with 35 lead changes and 352 overtakes. McLaren’s Lando Norris finished second, 0.639 seconds behind, with teammate Oscar Piastri third and newly crowned world champion Kimi Antonelli of Mercedes fourt
sports.content: Red Bull driver Max Verstappen won the Las Vegas Grand Prix on Saturday, claiming his 75th Formula 1 victory in a race with 35 lead changes and 352 overtakes. McLaren’s Lando Norris finished second, 0.639 seconds behind, with teammate Oscar Piastri third and newly crowned world champion Kimi Antonelli of Mercedes fourth. Verstappen repeatedly lost and reclaimed the lead in battles with Mercedes drivers George Russell and Antonelli, using the powerful slipstream on the long Strip straight and carefully managing his energy deployment. Russell hit a barrier while trying to pass Antonelli with three laps remaining and dropped to ninth. Antonelli then lost power late in the race, allowing both McLarens past. Ferrari teammates Lewis Hamilton and Charles Leclerc also collided while fighting for position. Leclerc received a 10-second penalty for causing the crash; Hamilton had earlier received a separate 10-second penalty for gaining an advantage after leaving the track. The result gives Verstappen a 40-point advantage over Russell in the battle for second in the drivers’ standings, with Qatar and Abu Dhabi left on the calendar. McLaren moved within nine points of Red Bull in the fight for third in the constructors’ standings. The Qatar Grand Prix is scheduled for Nov. 27-29.
sports.image_alt: Verstappen wins Las Vegas Grand Prix after 35 lead changes

sports.title: Manchester City draw 1-1 with Fulham as winless run reaches four
sports.summary: Manchester City drew 1-1 with Fulham at the Etihad Stadium on Saturday, extending their Premier League winless run to four matches. sports.content: Manchester City drew 1-1 with Fulham at the Etihad Stadium on Saturday, extending their Premier League winless run to four matches. Rodrigo Muniz put Fulham ahead in the 16th minute, and Elliot Anderson equalised with a volley in the 57th. City thought Erling Haaland had levelled earlier, but referee Thomas Bramall disallowed his close-range finish for a foul on goalkeeper Bernd Leno, and video assistant referee Sam Barrott upheld the decision. The point ended Fulham’s run of 20 straight defeats against City in all competitions, dating back to 2011, and extended the visitors’ unbeaten league run to five games. City, who had opened the season with seven league wins, have now taken one point from their last four matches. Home supporters booed the team at full-time. City face Napoli in the Champions League on Tuesday before visiting league leaders Arsenal next weekend. City manager Enzo Maresca says the team must address its slow starts, which he linked to a high proportion of the goals they have conceded.

sports.content: France beat Argentina 45-17 in Paris on Saturday, earning the bonus point needed to finish first in the Nations Championship’s northern pool and reach the inaugural final against South Africa. England’s 37-12 win over New Zealand earlier in the day meant France needed a win worth five competition points to overtake England. France led only 14-10 at half-time but pulled away after centre Kalvin Gourgues scored early in the second half. Argentina prop Mayco Vivas received a temporary red card for head contact, which was upgraded after review, and captain Julián Montoya was later sin-binned. Emilien Gailleton scored France’s fourth try in the 64th minute to secure the decisive bonus point. France added three more tries, including Gourgues’s second and Louis Bielle-Biarrey’s 31st in 30 Tests. France will play South Africa at Twickenham in London on Sunday, November 29, for the first title in the new competition. South Africa qualified as southern-pool leaders despite losing 20-17 to Ireland, with a losing bonus point helping them finish ahead of New Zealand. France beat the Springboks 21-19 in Paris on November 13.

sports.content: The Kansas City Current won their first National Women’s Soccer League championship with a 2-1 victory over the Washington Spirit at Audi Field on Nov. 21 in the club’s sixth season. Vanessa DiBernardo opened the scoring in the 54th minute with a rare goal directly from a corner kick, and Debinha added a breakaway goal in second-half stoppage time. Washington forward Trinity Rodman scored in the 98th minute, but Kansas City held on. Kansas City entered the playoffs as the No. 4 seed, a year after its record-setting 2025 regular season ended with an early postseason exit. The Current beat top-seeded Gotham FC in the semifinals before winning on the Spirit’s home field. Washington has now lost three consecutive championship games. DiBernardo was named championship MVP, while Washington’s late push failed to produce an equalizer. Kansas City plans a community celebration and champions’ march on Tuesday, Nov. 24.

sports.content: Edinburgh club Hearts beat Dundee 8-0 at Dens Park on Nov. 21, ending a run of three straight defeats, recording their biggest away league win and handing Dundee their heaviest home defeat. Hearts led 4-0 when Dundee defender Owen Bevan was sent off early in the second half; the visitors then added four more goals. Hearts host Monaco in the Conference League on Thursday. Hearts manager Wouter Vrancken cautioned that the win was only one performance, with nine more matches scheduled over the next 30 days. Dundee manager Steven Pressley said his side had lacked motivation and defensive grit, and accepted responsibility for preparing the team.

sports.content: Australia all-rounder Nikhil Chaudhary scored 66 and took two wickets as Australia chased down England’s target of 188 at the Melbourne Cricket Ground on November 21, winning the first of five Twenty20 internationals by three wickets with one ball to spare. Jack Edwards finished unbeaten on 25 from 11 balls, hitting the winning boundary to complete Australia’s record T20 international chase at the MCG and give the hosts a 1-0 series lead. England captain Harry Brook made 65 from 28 balls, helping his side post 187-9 after a 97-run stand with Tom Banton, who scored 39. Delhi-born Chaudhary dismissed Brook and Sam Curran before anchoring Australia’s reply in his fourth T20 international. Both teams fielded several new players. England’s Will Jacks left the field late in the chase with a hand injury. Brook is due to leave the T20 squad for England’s Test tour of South Africa, and the second match is scheduled for November 24 at Carrara.
